newsitem.title: UK: Ldn platinum surges, gold steady above $340.
newsitem.headline: Ldn platinum surges, gold steady above $340.

text.p: Gold reasserted itself above $340 an ounce on Thursday after having been struck by heavy selling earlier in the week, but dealers saw little upside prospects.
The price of platinum meanwhile surged by $13.50 an ounce on rumours that Russian exports to Japan could be further delayed by a gold swap deal with the Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS).
Platinum and palladium had a rollercoaster ride with conflicting remarks from Russian officials and Japanese traders on delayed Russian PGM sales to leading importer Japan.
"Maybe the Russians want to work out how much platinum and palladium they've got for exports first," said one dealer.
Prices jolted up after Russian Central Bank and finance ministry officials said they were unaware of a visit by the Central Bank to Japan next week to negotiate PGM exports.
Earlier prices slipped on news a mission might arrive at Tokyo to resume exports that have been delayed for four months.
Both platinum and palladium were marked sharply higher on the day. Platinum hit a high of $379.50 an ounce before slipping slightly while palladium gained $2.50 to $153.25/$154.25 an ounce.
Dealers said rumours that Russia was in talks with UBS to swap gold, held as collateral against a loan, with platinum and palladium could delay further the PGM negotiations with Japan.
The swap deal could not be immediately confirmed.
News that Russia plans a new approach to precious metals marketing to generate revenue raised some eyebrows among gold dealers, but there was no price reaction.
Bullion fixed marginally lower at $340.40 versus $341.20 and was indicated at $340.60/$341.10 in late trading, up $1.20.

Gold resurfaced above $340 after a selling bout tore through crucial support and send it to an intraday low of $337.50 on Wednesday. But selling has dried up and dealers expected the market to consolidate in the short-term before another downwturn.
"We are probably stuck in a $340-$345 range. Rallies above $345 are increasingly likely to be sold," said Ted Arnold, precious metals analyst at Merrill Lynch, earlier.
But despite the sturdier tone, a drop below $340 could not ruled out after a period of consolidation.
"The problem remains when and in what circumstances will investors be sucked back in and generate some sustained price upside," said Larry Kaplan of Flemings Global Mining Group.
Silver rallied to $4.85 early but only to retreat back to its earlier support level of $4.70 as upward momentum stalled.
"I think it was an aberration yesterday," said one dealer adding that gold's woes had made silver an attractive buy as silver stood rock steady but the move was not seen to last long.
Analysts said further challenges of resistance might only be possible if silver got a foothold above $4.88. By 1500 GMT, silver was quoted at $4.72/$4.74, down seven cents.
